issue.title: Remove RESTEasy exclusion

labels.name: area/dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

issue.body:
This instead adds the dependency in RESTEasy Common,
with an exclusion on the actual CP implementation.

This approach is much less problematic, as RESTEasy
has no knowledge of CP, so there is no chance these
classes can be accidently loaded unless CP is on the
classpath.

The current approach does not have this advatage so
problematic hacks have been used to try and stop it
being loaded, but this approach is much simpler.
Fixes #7809

issue.title: quarkus-mongodb-panache & quarkus-mailer in same project problem
issue.body:
I create a new quarkus project using maven:

mvn io.quarkus:quarkus-maven-plugin:1.3.1.Final:create \
    -DprojectGroupId=org.acme \
    -DprojectArtifactId=rest-json-quickstart \
    -DclassName="org.acme.rest.json.FruitResource" \
    -Dpath="/fruits" \
    -Dextensions="resteasy-jsonb"

then i add extension with:
mvn quarkus:add-extensions -Dextensions="mongodb-panache"

then i add extension with:
mvn quarkus:add-extensions -Dextensions="mailer"

When i launch quarkus in debug mode with:
mvn quarkus:dev

i get a class not found exception:
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.jboss.resteasy.context.ResteasyContextProvider

Now if i switch the 2 added extentions in pom.xml like this:
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-mailer</artifactId>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
      <artifactId>quarkus-mongodb-panache</artifactId>
    </dependency>

it works. Took me a bit of trial and error before i realized i just needed to switch my dependencies for it to work - but i assume it is not intended to work like that :-)
